set.formula: P_{\mathrm{axp}}(S;\mathcal T,F,\kappa,\mathbf v):=\neg\operatorname{CO}\!\left(\llbracket\left(\bigwedge_{i\in S}x_i=v_i\right)\land(\kappa(\mathbf x)\ne c)\rrbracket_{\mathcal T}\right).
P_{\mathrm{cxp}}(S;\mathcal T,F,\kappa,\mathbf v):=\operatorname{CO}\!\left(\llbracket\left(\bigwedge_{i\in F\setminus S}x_i=v_i\right)\land(\kappa(\mathbf x)\ne c)\rrbracket_{\mathcal T}\right).

set.quote: The security of a steganographic system is quantified in terms of the relative entropy (or discrimination) between the distributions of C and S, which yields bounds on the detection capability of any adversary.
set.relation: Restated in anwar2026decision (App. D, Proposition D.1) with the arguments of the divergence reversed, as D_KL(P_1||P_0) <= epsilon; there the binary-detection special case of the steganographic gap satisfies normalized gap = 1 - TV >= 1 - sqrt(epsilon/2).

set.quote: In a perfectly secure stegosystem, Eve cannot distinguish the two distributions and has no information at all about the presence of an embedded message.

set.relation: Umbrella for current-state, initial-state, initial-final, K-step, infinite-step and pre-opacity; the paper contrasts its infinite-step form ('always not know') with diagnosability ('always eventually know'); related to noninterference; several classes expressed as hyperproperties (HyperLTL).
Limit of K-step opacity as K goes to infinity; an 'always not know' requirement, which the paper contrasts with diagnosability ('always eventually know').

Contrasted in the paper with infinite-step opacity ('always eventually know' against 'always not know'); related to detectability, observability and prognosability. The paper does not mention monitorability: the analogy (a monitor inferring misbehavior from partial observations) is the map's.

notes: KaTeX cannot size \llbracket with \left; same formula without the sizing. Cachin rows checked against the author's revised full text (cachin.com, 2004): divergence is D(P_C||P_S). Yin never calls diagnosability a dual.
